# InkToolbar

Header: `winui/ui/media/InkToolbar.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/media/InkToolbar.hpp`.

A row of ink tools bound to a [ui::InkCanvasControl](ink-canvas.md#uiinkcanvascontrol). By default it holds a ballpoint pen, a pencil, a highlighter and an eraser, in that order.

Clicking a tool makes it the active tool and sets the target canvas up for it. A pen sets its drawing attributes and Inking mode, and the eraser sets Erasing mode. Clicking the active tool again opens its flyout. A pen's flyout picks a color from the pen's palette and a stroke width with a slider, over a sample stroke. The palette has 30 colors, six for the highlighter, and the width goes from 1 to 24 DIPs, 12 to 64 for the highlighter. The eraser's flyout switches the target canvas between its stroke and point erasers ([InkCanvasControl::set_erase_mode()](ink-canvas.md#set_erase_mode)) and offers "Erase all ink", which clears the canvas. The toolbar is one tab stop. The arrow keys move between the tools, and Space or Enter does what a click does.

The app can add tools of its own after the built-in ones. A custom pen draws with attributes it makes from the picked color and width. A custom tool turns the canvas's inking off, so the app handles its input through on_unprocessed_input(), for example for a lasso. A custom toggle sits after the tools. [add_stencil_button()](#add_stencil_button) adds the button that shows a ruler or a protractor on the canvas. [`ui::InkToolbar`](#uiinktoolbar) is the declarative form.

Example: 
```cpp
auto  canvas  = std::make_unique<ui::InkCanvasControl>();
auto  toolbar = std::make_unique<ui::InkToolbarControl>();
toolbar->set_target_ink_canvas(canvas.get());
toolbar->on_active_tool_changed([](ui::InkToolbarTool tool)
                                { std::println("tool {}", static_cast<int>(tool)); });
toolbar->set_active_tool(ui::InkToolbarTool::Highlighter); // the canvas now highlights

auto stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
stack->add(std::move(toolbar));
canvas->set_height(300.0f);
stack->add(std::move(canvas));
window.set_content(std::move(stack));
```

## `ui::InkToolbar`

A row of ink tools for an [InkCanvas](ink-canvas.md#uiinkcanvas). Builds a [ui::InkToolbarControl](#uiinktoolbarcontrol), whose description lists the tools and their flyouts.

[`.target`](#uiinktoolbar-target) names the canvas by its handle, and the canvas can be built before or after the toolbar. Until the canvas exists, the tools only change the toolbar's own state. The active tool's attributes reach the canvas once it is linked. [`.active_tool = tool`](#uiinktoolbar-active_tool) is two-way.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Control<ui::InkCanvas>       canvas;
ui::Property<ui::InkToolbarTool> tool{ui::InkToolbarTool::BallpointPen};

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.spacing = 8, .content = {
    ui::InkToolbar{
        .tools                = {ui::InkToolbarTool::BallpointPen, ui::InkToolbarTool::Highlighter,
                                 ui::InkToolbarTool::Eraser},
        .active_tool          = tool,
        .target               = canvas, // the canvas draws with the active tool
        .horizontal_alignment = ui::Alignment::Leading,
        .accessibility        = {.name = "Drawing tools"},
    },
    ui::Border{.background = ui::colors::White,
               .height     = 280.0f,
               .content    = ui::InkCanvas{.control = canvas}},
}});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::InkToolbar{
    .tools, .custom_pens, .custom_tools, .custom_toggles, .stencil_button, .active_tool,
    .orientation, .button_flyout_placement, .target, .style, .margin, .width, .height,
    .min_width, .min_height, .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment,
    .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .enabled, .accessibility,
    .on_active_tool_changed, .on_ink_drawing_attributes_changed, .on_erase_all_clicked,
    .on_stencil_button_checked_changed, .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus,
    .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control
}
```

## `ui::InkToolbarControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`.

A row of ink tools bound to a [ui::InkCanvasControl](ink-canvas.md#uiinkcanvascontrol). By default it holds a ballpoint pen, a pencil, a highlighter and an eraser, in that order.

Clicking a tool makes it the active tool and sets the target canvas up for it. A pen sets its drawing attributes and Inking mode, and the eraser sets Erasing mode. Clicking the active tool again opens its flyout. A pen's flyout picks a color from the pen's palette and a stroke width with a slider, over a sample stroke. The palette has 30 colors, six for the highlighter, and the width goes from 1 to 24 DIPs, 12 to 64 for the highlighter. The eraser's flyout switches the target canvas between its stroke and point erasers ([InkCanvasControl::set_erase_mode()](ink-canvas.md#set_erase_mode)) and offers "Erase all ink", which clears the canvas. The toolbar is one tab stop. The arrow keys move between the tools, and Space or Enter does what a click does.

The app can add tools of its own after the built-in ones. A custom pen draws with attributes it makes from the picked color and width. A custom tool turns the canvas's inking off, so the app handles its input through on_unprocessed_input(), for example for a lasso. A custom toggle sits after the tools. [add_stencil_button()](#add_stencil_button) adds the button that shows a ruler or a protractor on the canvas. [`ui::InkToolbar`](#uiinktoolbar) is the declarative form.

Example: 
```cpp
auto  canvas  = std::make_unique<ui::InkCanvasControl>();
auto  toolbar = std::make_unique<ui::InkToolbarControl>();
toolbar->set_target_ink_canvas(canvas.get());
toolbar->on_active_tool_changed([](ui::InkToolbarTool tool)
                                { std::println("tool {}", static_cast<int>(tool)); });
toolbar->set_active_tool(ui::InkToolbarTool::Highlighter); // the canvas now highlights

auto stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
stack->add(std::move(toolbar));

stack->add(std::move(canvas));

```

### InkToolbarControl

```cpp
InkToolbarControl(std::span<const InkToolbarTool> tools = AllTools)
```

A toolbar with a button for each of `tools`, in that order. A repeated tool appears once. The first is the active tool.

## class InkToolbarToolButtonControl

Derives from `ui::Element`, `ui::SelectionItemProvider`, `ui::ExpandCollapseProvider`.

One tool button of a [ui::InkToolbarControl](#uiinktoolbarcontrol): a pen, the eraser or another tool. The toolbar makes these. Reach one through [InkToolbarControl::tool_button()](#tool_button).

The button is a 36 DIP square with the tool's glyph. A pen button also shows its selected color in the glyph, and holds the palette and the stroke width its flyout edits. The eraser button holds whether its flyout offers "Erase all ink". The active tool's button is drawn selected, with a small chevron toward the flyout it opens on a second click.

Example: 
```cpp
auto                             toolbar = std::make_unique<ui::InkToolbarControl>();
ui::InkToolbarToolButtonControl* pen     = toolbar->tool_button(ui::InkToolbarTool::BallpointPen);
pen->set_selected_brush_index(7);       // red, in the default palette
pen->set_selected_stroke_width(6.0f);   // within min_stroke_width()..max_stroke_width()
```

```

```

## struct InkToolbarCustomButton

How a custom button of a [ui::InkToolbarControl](#uiinktoolbarcontrol) looks and what it does. The button is a custom pen, a custom tool or a custom toggle. Each field applies to the kinds its comment names.

The callables are std::function, so they can be copied. The spec lists custom buttons in a braced list, which copies its entries.

Example: 
```cpp
// A calligraphy pen: a flat nib a third as wide as it is tall.
auto toolbar = std::make_unique<ui::InkToolbarControl>();
toolbar->add_custom_pen({.name  = "Calligraphy pen",
                         .icon  = ui::IconGlyph{0xEDFB},
                         .pen   = [](ui::Color color, float width)
                         {
                             return ui::InkDrawingAttributes{.color   = color,
                                                             .size    = {width / 3.0f, width},
                                                             .pen_tip = ui::InkPenTip::Rectangle};
                         }});
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `std::string` |  | Its tool tip and accessible name. Every kind. |
| `icon` | `IconSource` |  | The icon it shows: a [Symbol](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#symbol), a glyph, a path or a picture. A glyph of the default symbol font takes the theme's icon font. Every kind. |
| `configuration` | `std::function<Spec()>` |  | What a click on the active custom pen or tool opens in its flyout. Without it, a custom pen opens the pens' color and size flyout, and a custom tool opens nothing. |
| `pen` | `std::function<InkDrawingAttributes(Color color, float width)>` |  | What a custom pen draws with, made from the color and width picked in its flyout. Without it, the pen draws with a round nib of that color and width. |
| `on_checked_changed` | `std::function<void(bool checked)>` |  | Called when a custom toggle turns on or off, with the new state. |

## struct InkToolbarStencilChangedArgs

What an [InkToolbar](#uiinktoolbar)'s `on_stencil_button_checked_changed` gets: whether the stencil button is on, and the stencil it shows.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `checked` | `bool` | `false` | The button is on and the stencil shows. |
| `kind` | `InkToolbarStencilKind` | `InkToolbarStencilKind::Ruler` | The stencil the button selects. |

## class InkToolbarToggleButtonControl

Derives from `ui::Element`, `ui::ToggleProvider`.

A toggle button on a [ui::InkToolbarControl](#uiinktoolbarcontrol). It turns on or off and sits after the tools. Add one with [InkToolbarControl::add_custom_toggle()](#add_custom_toggle).

Example: 
```cpp
// A toggle that lets touch draw as well as the pen and the mouse.
auto canvas  = std::make_unique<ui::InkCanvasControl>();
auto toolbar = std::make_unique<ui::InkToolbarControl>();
ui::InkToolbarToggleButtonControl* touch =
    toolbar->add_custom_toggle({.name = "Touch writing", .icon = ui::IconGlyph{0xED5F}});
touch->on_checked_changed([ink = canvas.get()](bool on) {
    ink->set_input_device_types(on ? ui::PointerDeviceTypes::All
                                   : ui::PointerDeviceTypes::Pen | ui::PointerDeviceTypes::Mouse);
});
```

## class InkToolbarStencilButtonControl

Derives from `ui::Element`, `ui::ToggleProvider`, `ui::ExpandCollapseProvider`.

The stencil button of a [ui::InkToolbarControl](#uiinktoolbarcontrol), which shows the ruler or the protractor on the target canvas. Add it with [InkToolbarControl::add_stencil_button()](#add_stencil_button).

A click while it is off turns it on and shows the stencil picked last, the ruler at first. A click while it is on opens its flyout, which picks the ruler or the protractor. Picking the one showing hides it and turns the button off. With only one of the two offered, it is a plain toggle with no flyout.

Example: 
```cpp
auto                                toolbar  = std::make_unique<ui::InkToolbarControl>();
ui::InkToolbarStencilButtonControl* stencils = toolbar->add_stencil_button();
stencils->set_selected_stencil(ui::InkToolbarStencilKind::Protractor);
toolbar->set_stencil_button_checked(true); // the protractor shows on the canvas
```

## Enumerations

### InkToolbarTool

```cpp
enum class InkToolbarTool
```

A tool on a [ui::InkToolbarControl](#uiinktoolbarcontrol).

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `BallpointPen` | A round, solid pen. |
| `Pencil` | Pencil ink. |
| `Highlighter` | A wide, translucent chisel nib. |
| `Eraser` | The stroke eraser, with "Erase all ink" in its flyout. |
| `CustomPen` | A pen the app defines ([InkToolbarControl::add_custom_pen()](#add_custom_pen)). |
| `CustomTool` | A tool the app implements ([InkToolbarControl::add_custom_tool()](#add_custom_tool)). |

### InkToolbarStencilKind

```cpp
enum class InkToolbarStencilKind
```

Which stencil the stencil button shows on the canvas.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Ruler` | The ruler ([InkCanvasControl::set_ruler()](ink-canvas.md#set_ruler)). |
| `Protractor` | The protractor ([InkCanvasControl::set_protractor()](ink-canvas.md#set_protractor)). |

### InkToolbarButtonFlyoutPlacement

```cpp
enum class InkToolbarButtonFlyoutPlacement
```

Which side of its button a tool's flyout opens on.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Auto` | Below the button, the same as Bottom. |
| `Top` | Above the button, left edges lined up. |
| `Bottom` | Below the button, left edges lined up. |
| `Left` | Left of the button, centered. |
| `Right` | Right of the button, centered. |
